rule.text: indexable episodes in lineage_seq order, at positions round(i*(n-1)/(target-1)) for i in 0..target-1

determinism.polish_note: 6 episodes sampled twice from the model; identical bytes are the absence of drift in one sample, not a determinism guarantee — the second call of a real provider is what a ship decision needs and no key was reachable here

template.note: arm A is a byte function of the delta document: no clock, no locale, no terminal probe, so a golden test can bless it

files.polish.md: arm B - the model's full polish of arm A, prompt prompt/polish.md
files.polish2.md: arm B second sample, same prompt, for the determinism measurement (6 episodes)
files.template.md: arm A - rendered by recommender.narrative.template, not by the model
files.why.md: arm C - the model's single why-sentence, prompt prompt/why.md

llm_arm_provenance.how: The model that ran this spike generated the arm B and arm C texts itself, in-session, from the pinned prompts in ../prompt/ and the recorded citation index in ../evidence/. There is no API key, provider SDK or outbound endpoint in the spike sandbox, so the arms are recorded artefacts on disk rather than live calls, and re-running the spike re-reads them instead of asking the model again - which is the property you want in a report a CI job can check.

model.harness: pi coding agent, reasoning level medium

what_that_costs: cost and latency for arms B and C are MODELLED from recorded character counts at a reference price band (spike.REFERENCE), not measured against a bill or a clock; the ship decision is gated on re-measuring them against a real provider endpoint
sampling parameters are the harness's, not chosen for this experiment, and cannot be re-set

one base model authored the narratives, the resamples and the three reviewer passes, so arm quality and panel ratings share a bias the panel cannot see; the mechanical audit in audit.py is the part of the measurement that does not depend on that model being any good

the author knew the audit's rules, because the same session wrote them - the strongest reason the zero hallucination count is read as an upper bound on a disciplined arm, not as a rate a stranger would hit

agreement.note: three rubric passes of one base model: this is a floor on disagreement, not a measurement of human disagreement

per_episode.subject: reco-2uo: the first five minutes — a repository that ships in the binary, an estimate that converges, and no shrugs anywhere (e5.9)

question: does an optional LLM narrative polish beat the deterministic template on accuracy, usefulness and trustworthiness, with hallucinations held at zero

verdict.decision: ship-nothing-yet: arm A is e4.7's narrative; the net-llm polish seam stays unwired (no consumer, no flag, no code path) until every gate in the decision issue is met
gates: hallucinated claims at zero on >=100 episodes and >=3 repositories, with an adversarial arm
a measured win on trustworthiness as well as usefulness, from three human reviewers
cost and latency measured against a real provider, and a byte-identical offline fallback
byte-stable exports (e5.7) survive a polished narrative, or that guarantee is dropped on purpose
citation preservation enforced by the renderer, not instructed to the model
verdict.why: usefulness rose (2.23 -> 4.40) while trustworthiness fell (4.667 -> 4.000) and coverage halved (0.61 -> 0.32); ADR-001 §8 non-goal 6 asks for a win on trust AND usefulness with hallucinations at zero, and the readability gap the polish arm closes is a template bug worth fixing in the template - see docs/concepts/narrative-polish.md §7
